To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

sex specific genetic effects contribute to human phenotypes, and that genetic association studies that ignore sex differences in their design and analysis will fail to identify a large proportion of the genes responsible for common disease.

(i) sex specific genetic effects are common in human disease, (ii) the genetic architecture of human diseases is likely to be sex specific, (iii) the underlying mechanism is differential regulation of genes by sex steroid hormones, and (iv) the sex specific effects in disease genes can be detected in genetic association studies.
